summary: Geometry, beat-locked expansion rate and both dial mappings match the original exactly, but the port renders the starburst about 4x darker, half as many lit pixels, and with its brightness/saturation relationship inverted — vivid full-saturation 255 fill on the original versus a sparse, pastel, mostly-black field on the port.
observations: Both sides compile and run with no errors; both report wantsSensors: true and are fed the beat120 synth signal (sensorModel beat120 on every run). With --sensors off BOTH sides render pure black (mean 0, motion 0) — identical graceful/dead degradation, no divergence there.
Control surface matches exactly: both sides expose sliderHowManyLeaders (slider, label HowManyLeaders) and sliderRainbow (slider, label Rainbow). No missing/extra/renamed/retyped control.

Shape of the pattern (both sides): a mirrored starburst that spawns a new outward-travelling front from each 'leader' centre on every 2 Hz beat; on a 60 px strip the strip tiles cleanly into N equal segments, and the waterfall reads as a chevron/diamond lattice. The lattice slopes are visually identical between sides (see lead-0 waterfalls) — same expansion geometry.

Front speed matches and is fps-invariant on BOTH sides: with 1 leader (sliderHowManyLeaders=0) the outermost lit pixel advances ~4 px per 0.5 s beat on the original and ~5 px per 0.5 s on the port, and the same per-second rate is measured at --fps 20 and --fps 40 (f0-10/f0-20/f0-40 dumps). Neither side is frame-rate coupled in its expansion.

BRIGHTNESS (headline): at sliderHowManyLeaders=0 over 100 dumped frames spanning 10 s (lead0-mask), original mean pixel value 96.8 vs port 25.5 — the port is 3.8x dimmer. Original holds 19.6 of 60 pixels at full 255 on an average frame; the port holds 1.2. On the untouched default over 120 s at 20 fps the ratio is milder but persistent: orig meanBrightness 93, port 55.

LIT COVERAGE: original lights 30.6/60 pixels per frame, port 15.4/60 (lead=0, 100 frames). The lit masks overlap poorly — mean IoU 0.271, and a ±20-frame time-lag scan never lifts it above 0.34, so this is not a phase offset, it is genuinely less lit area.

SATURATION / colour ladder inverted: mean HSV saturation of lit pixels is 0.950 (orig) vs 0.716 (port); saturation histogram [0-.2,.2-.4,.4-.6,.6-.8,.8-1] = orig [0,150,60,72,2780] vs port [0,394,200,152,794]. Crucially the two sides put the washed-out pixels in opposite places. Original frame at t=4.05 s (lead=0): 12 px at sat 1.00 / value 255 plus a long full-saturation decaying tail (values 133,122,86,71,68,48,...,13) covering most of the strip, with only 2 whitened 'head' pixels (sat 0.39 @ V=255). Port at the same instant: only 2 bright pixels (sat 0.23 @ V=251), 6 mid pixels (sat 0.45-0.63 @ V≈97-101) and 6 fully-saturated but nearly-black pixels (sat 1.00 @ V=21-22). So on the original bright==saturated and only the leading head is whitened; on the port bright==pastel and only the dim residue is saturated.

TAIL LENGTH: the original's decaying trail spans essentially the whole strip (values fading 255 -> 6 over ~30 px each side of the centre) and the strip only goes fully dark at the very end of a burst; the port's trail is 3-6 px wide and the rest of the strip is exactly 0,0,0. This is what produces both the coverage and the brightness gap.

The gap widens with rig size: at --pixels 180 (lead=0.4) the original holds 100 px at full 255 and mean value 147, the port holds 10 px at 255 and mean value 34. At --pixels 30 the two are much closer (orig 20 full / meanV 170, port 10 full / meanV 84). The port's bright plateau does not scale with strip length the way the original's does.

UNTOUCHED-DEFAULT leader count differs: with no controls set, the original tiles 60 px with spatial period 10 (6 starburst centres) on 114 of 120 sampled frames; the port tiles with period 15 (4 centres) on every sampled frame. Dialed, the counts agree exactly (see dials).

RHYTHM: over 120 s at 20 fps the original's motion autocorrelation shows a clean 0.5 s beat peak (r=0.75 at lag 10) and a dominant 6.00 s super-cycle (r=0.88 at lag 120, 0.80 at 240). The port's 0.5 s peak is only r=0.32 and its dominant period is 2.00 s (r=0.67); it has no 6 s super-cycle (r=0.23 at lag 120). Motion-peak rates are similar (orig 5.01/s, port 5.72/s) but the interval histograms differ: orig favours 0.20/0.10/0.30 s spacings, port favours 0.10/0.15/0.25 s. The port reacts to the beat (fronts do spawn every 0.5 s) but its whole-rig rhythm is less beat-coherent and lacks the original's long cycle.

HUE ROTATION: the original's hue walks smoothly and linearly at ~90 deg/s, locking to a 4.00 s cycle (hue-cos autocorrelation r=0.95 at lag 80 frames @20 fps, 0.91 at 160, 0.88 at 240) — exactly the beat120 melody's 8-step / 4 s scale period. The port walks at ~85 deg/s and its best hue-cos lag is 4.50 s (r=0.70), i.e. ~12% slow and much less phase-coherent.

Both sides are seed-independent (seed 1 / 7 / 1234 give identical stats on both sides) and neither dies: over --skip 60 --seconds 20 both are brightnessTrend steady (orig mean 93, port 54), same ratio as the opening window. No decay-to-black, no freeze; zeroMotionFrames is 1 on both over 2400-frame runs.

Warm-up regime (first ~1.6 s of the timeline): the original flashes the whole strip at full brightness in a saturated rainbow chevron before settling; the port shows the same chevron shape in the same slot but at ~60% value and heavily desaturated (survey/survey240 top band, baseline waterfall top rows). No other regimes exist — the 240 s survey at 10 fps shows one homogeneous texture after that point on both sides.

dials.name: sliderHowManyLeaders
dials.origEffect: Sets the number of starburst centres tiled across the strip, and hence overall brightness. Measured centre counts on 60 px at v=0/0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8/1 are 1/3/5/1/3/12 (spatial periods 60/20/12/60/20/5) — a non-monotonic mapping, but reproducible. Mean brightness over 12 s rises monotonically 48 -> 77 -> 102 -> 115 -> 117 -> 122 across v=0/0.15/0.35/0.65/0.85/1.
dials.portEffect: Identical centre counts at every probed value (1/3/5/1/3/12, same spatial periods), and the same monotonic brightness ramp in the same direction: 19 -> 35 -> 61 -> 90 -> 98 -> 102. The mapping from dial value to leader count is an exact match; only the absolute brightness is ~50-60% of the original's at every setting. Probe maxDelta 56.41 / maxDeltaLit 84.24 (orig 73.62 / 82.61).

dials.name: sliderRainbow
dials.origEffect: A binary switch, not a continuous knob: values 0 and 0.5 render byte-identical, values 0.6/0.7/0.8/0.9/0.95/0.99/1.0 all render byte-identical to each other, so the threshold is exactly at v>0.5 . OFF = the whole strip shares one hue at a time (1 distinct hue per frame), rotating over time. ON = the hue is spread across the burst rings, ~12-15 distinct hues per frame in 24-degree steps. Mean per-frame pixel delta between OFF and ON: 25-93.
dials.portEffect: Same binary structure and the SAME threshold (0 == 0.5, 0.6..1.0 all identical, switch at v>0.5). OFF = single hue per frame; ON = hue spread across rings, but only ~10 distinct hues per frame in 36-degree steps (the original uses 24-degree steps over more rings) — a direct consequence of the port's shorter burst tail. The visible effect is much weaker: mean per-frame delta between OFF and ON is only 8-15 (orig 25-93), and probe maxDelta 15.59 vs the original's 78.15.

feedback: Brightness is the biggest gap: at the same dial settings the port's mean pixel value is ~3.8x lower than the original's (96.8 vs 25.5 at HowManyLeaders=0, 60 px, 10 s window). The original keeps ~20 of 60 pixels pinned at 255 on an average frame; the port keeps ~1. Scale the burst's peak output up so the body of the burst renders at full 255, not just the head pixel.

The trail/afterglow decays far too fast spatially. The original's fading tail reaches from the burst centre to the strip ends (a smooth ramp 255 -> ~6 over ~30 px per side, so ~31/60 pixels lit per frame); the port's tail is 3-6 px wide and everything beyond it is exactly 0,0,0 (~15/60 lit). Lengthen the tail so lit coverage roughly doubles.

The saturation/brightness relationship is inverted. On the original, the bright body of the burst is FULLY saturated (S=1.0 at V=255) and only the 2 leading 'head' pixels are whitened (S≈0.39-0.86 at V=255). On the port the bright pixels are the washed-out ones (S=0.23-0.63 at V≈100-251) while the S=1.0 pixels are all nearly black (V=6-40). Apply the whitening only to the leading edge and keep the trail at full saturation.

Untouched (no controls set) the port draws 4 starburst centres on a 60 px strip where the original draws 6 (spatial period 15 vs 10). Every explicitly-dialed value of HowManyLeaders matches exactly (1/3/5/1/3/12 centres at 0/0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8/1), so it is only the pattern's internal default leader value that is off — bring it in line with the original's default.

Rainbow mode spreads too coarsely: with sliderRainbow>0.5 the original paints ~12-15 hues across the burst in 24-degree steps; the port paints ~10 hues in 36-degree steps. Fixing the tail length (feedback #2) probably fixes this too, since the hue step appears tied to the number of visible rings — but verify the step size ends up at 24 degrees.

Hue rotation is ~12% slow and less coherent: the original's hue cycle autocorrelates cleanly at 4.00 s (r=0.95), locking to the melody's 8-step / 4 s scale; the port's best lag is 4.50 s at r=0.70. Tie the hue advance to the melody step (maxFrequency staircase) rather than to a free-running timer.

Whole-rig rhythm is under-modulated: the original's motion series autocorrelates at 0.5 s with r=0.75 and has a 6.00 s super-cycle (r=0.88); the port scores r=0.32 at 0.5 s, has no 6 s cycle (r=0.23) and its dominant period is 2.00 s. The port does spawn one front per beat, so the beat detection itself is fine — the missing beat contrast comes from the missing bright fill, so re-check this after the brightness/tail fixes before chasing it separately.

Non-issues, confirmed matching — do not 'fix' these: front expansion speed (~4-5 px per 0.5 s beat, fps-invariant on both sides at 20 and 40 fps), leader-count scaling with rig size (5 centres on 180 px on both), the sliderRainbow threshold (exactly v>0.5 on both), seed independence, and the all-black --sensors off behaviour (identical on both).
